text.title: Laravel Umbrella Examples
text.summary: Worked example: taking a facade-heavy legacy service to constructor injection, provider bindings and cacheable config — the framework-fundamentals half of this methodology applied end-to-end.

example.context: Legacy Laravel 11 app. `PaymentService` calls `Mail::send`, `Log::info`, `Cache::get` and reads `env('STRIPE_KEY')` directly; every test needs `Mail::fake()` plus `Queue::fake()`; `config:cache` breaks production.
example.walk: Step 1: define `Contracts\MailService`, `Contracts\CacheService` and use PSR-3 `LoggerInterface`. Step 2: `PaymentServiceProvider::register()` binds `MailService` → `SendgridMailService` and `CacheService` → `RedisCacheService`; the provider is registered. Step 3: `env('STRIPE_KEY')` becomes `config('stripe.key')`, backed by a new `config/stripe.php`. Step 4: `PaymentService` constructor-injects all three contracts; `Mail::send(...)` becomes `$this->mail->send(...)`. Step 5: the repeated terms-of-service check becomes an `EnforceTos` middleware on the route group, and the deploy script gains `route:cache` + `config:cache`.
example.output: Unit tests run with plain PHPUnit mocks and no framework boot; `config:cache` and `route:cache` both succeed; the first request after deploy resolves every binding.

example.note: The one place a contract is wired to an implementation, per `contract-bind-in-provider`.
Services read `config('stripe.key')`; the frozen cache then holds real values instead of nulls.
